title: KSP-FF K=5 vs K=50 Overload Audit (Final Report)

code_audit_finding.fairness_issue: The legacy comparison confounded K value with selector policy. K5 used plain FF while K50 used highest-mod FF.

conclusion.details: The observed K50>K5 blocking is overwhelmingly caused by the fact that legacy ksp_ff (K5) uses plain First-Fit while legacy ksp_ff_k50_hops uses highest-modulation First-Fit. Under strict same-selector conditions, K5 and K50 are statistically tied (plain: 7.46% vs 7.92%; highest-mod: 9.93% vs 9.93%). The highest-mod selector harms overload-dominated performance because it raises feasible counts, causing PPO-C to select more split-0 (heavy edge-offload) assignments and concentrate load on server 0.

paper_recommendation.honest_explanation_k50_not_better: In our compute-optical setting, blocking is dominated by server overload. The legacy KSP-FF K50 label actually denotes a highest-modulation selector, which is not directly comparable to the plain KSP-FF K5 baseline. When K is varied while holding the selector fixed, K50 does not outperform K5; the apparent K50 penalty is a selector effect, not a path-horizon effect.
paper_recommendation.honest_explanation_v13_better: v1.3 (PPO-C + learned R ranker) outperforms the fair KSP-FF K50 baseline because it is optimized for the joint compute-optical objective, not because K50 paths are harmful. The ranker avoids the server-overload trap that the highest-modulation heuristic induces.
